# Skill Forge

> Skill Forge turns scattered notes, documents or a single idea into a complete,
> detailed skill for AI agents. Each skill is a Markdown file with a numbered
> procedure, rules, examples, common mistakes and a final checklist. Skills can
> be downloaded as `.md` or published to a public marketplace.

Skill Forge is a web application and a CLI. Generation uses OpenRouter as the AI
gateway, with automatic fallback across free models. The marketplace is public:
anyone can browse, search and download skills without an account; publishing
requires signing in with GitHub.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://skillforge.cc.cd/): what the service does, with a before and
  after example of raw notes turned into a skill.
- [Live demo](https://skillforge.cc.cd/demo): paste text and get a real skill
  preview with no account.
- [Marketplace](https://skillforge.cc.cd/marketplace): browse, search and sort
  the published skills.
- [Tags](https://skillforge.cc.cd/tags): the skills grouped by topic.
- [Create from material](https://skillforge.cc.cd/create/from-skills): merge up
  to 20 files or pasted text into one skill.
- [Create from scratch](https://skillforge.cc.cd/create/from-scratch): a 6-field
  wizard (name, domain, goal, tone, constraints, examples).

## Output format

Every generated skill contains, in order: YAML frontmatter (`name`,
`description`), when to use it, when not to use it, prerequisites, procedure,
rules and constraints, examples with input and expected output, common mistakes,
missing information with the questions to ask, and a final checklist.

Where the source material is incomplete, the generator does not invent facts: it
lists the missing information and the questions whose answers would close it.
